newsitem.title: USA: Mercantile, Mark Twain say to merge.
newsitem.headline: Mercantile, Mark Twain say to merge.

text.p: Mercantile Bancorp Inc and Mark Twain Bancshares Inc, both bank holding companies based in St. Louis, Mo., said they signed a definitive merger agreement structured as an $855-million tax-free exchange.
Mark Twain directors unanimously approved the transaction and have indicated that they will vote their shares in favor of the merger, the companies said.
Under the terms of the agreement, Mark Twain shareholders will receive 0.9520 share of Mercantile common stock for each share of Mark Twain common stock, the banks said.

The merger will be accounted for as a pooling of interests. Based on Friday's closing price for Mercantile common stock of $52.125, the transaction is valued at $49.62 per share of Mark Twain common stock, they said.
"Both Mercantile and Mark Twain will rescind all previously announced share repurchase programs," they said.
Mercantile may repurchase up to 700,000 shares in the open market from time to time depending upon market conditions and other factors, the companies said.
Upon completion of the merger, Alvin Siteman, chairman of Mark Twain Bancshares, would become chairman of Mercantile Bank of St. Louis, and join the Mercantile Bancorp board.

John Dubinsky, president and chief executive of Mark Twain Bancshares, would become president and chief executive of Mercantile Bank of St. Louis and a member of Mercantile's management executive committee.

"This merger ... brings together the strengths of two high-performing organizations and solidifies Mercantile's position as the largest locally managed, and independently owned banking operation in St. Louis and the state of Missouri," said Thomas Jacobsen, Mercantile chairman and chief executive.
Plans call for the merger to be completed in the second quarter of 1997, the companies said.
Mercantile has assests of about $18.2 billion and Twain of about $3.1 billion, they said.
